- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often overpredicts recovery; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated upward momentum; cap forecast growth at 2–4% for next 3–5 periods.  
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting back to 60–65 after 65+), check sentiment for reversal signals — if sentiment is neutral or turning negative, reduce forecast slope.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or mixed.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead in direction of sentiment momentum.
